paragraphs.title: Arrival at the Jordan and distance instructions

easy.question: From where did Joshua and the Israelites set out at the start of the chapter?
answers: Jericho
Shittim
The watch
easy.explanation: The verse opens 'And they removed from Shittim' — they left Shittim.

easy.question: How many days passed until the officers went through the camp?
answers: Three days
One day
Seven days
easy.explanation: The text says 'after three days, that the officers went through the host' — three days.

easy.question: Who is carrying the ark of the covenant according to the verse?
answers: Selected tribes
Joshua and his sons
The priests, the Levites
easy.explanation: The verse states 'the priests the Levites bearing it' — the priests (Levites) carry it.

medium.question: What does the word 'cubit' mean in the phrase 'about two thousand cubits by measure'?
answers: An ancient unit of length (cubit)
A unit of weight
A type of ceremonial garment
medium.explanation: 'Cubit' here denotes an ancient unit of length; the context is distance ('about two thousand cubits').

medium.question: Why did Joshua command the people to move from their places and follow the ark?
answers: To precede it and prepare for battle
To follow the ark's direction and go the right way
To remain and fight at the camp
medium.explanation: His instruction 'you shall remove from your place and go after it' shows the people were to move following the ark to know the way.

medium.question: What did Joshua command when the ark of the covenant was shown to the people?
answers: That the people should lead a procession before it
That they should not come too near it and should walk behind it
That they should remain and fast until further instruction
medium.explanation: The verses indicate the people should observe the ark, keep a distance, and go after it rather than approach it.

challenge.question: What was the practical role of the 'officers' who went through the camp?
answers: To serve as discipline and order and prepare the people to set out
To be bearers of the ark
To perform sacrifice rituals before the crossing
challenge.explanation: The officers walked through the camp to arrange and prepare the people for departure; they did not bear the ark or perform sacrifices.

challenge.question: Approximately how much distance does 'about two thousand cubits' represent in modern terms?
answers: About 100 meters
About 10 kilometers
About 1 kilometer
challenge.explanation: Two thousand cubits (estimating a cubit ~0.5 m) is roughly 1,000 meters — about one kilometer.

challenge.question: What does the sentence 'for ye have not passed this way heretofore' suggest about the Israelites' experience with this road?
answers: That they had traveled this road many times before
That it was a road they had not gone before
That they had allegedly passed there only two days ago
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates they had not traveled this way previously — it was new to them.

questions.question: What was the practical role of the 'officers' who went through the camp?
answers: To serve as discipline and order and prepare the people to set out
To be bearers of the ark
To perform sacrifice rituals before the crossing
questions.explanation: The officers walked through the camp to arrange and prepare the people for departure; they did not bear the ark or perform sacrifices.

questions.question: Approximately how much distance does 'about two thousand cubits' represent in modern terms?
answers: About 100 meters
About 10 kilometers
About 1 kilometer
questions.explanation: Two thousand cubits (estimating a cubit ~0.5 m) is roughly 1,000 meters — about one kilometer.

questions.question: What does the sentence 'for ye have not passed this way heretofore' suggest about the Israelites' experience with this road?
answers: That they had traveled this road many times before
That it was a road they had not gone before
That they had allegedly passed there only two days ago
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates they had not traveled this way previously — it was new to them.

easy.question: What did Joshua command the people in verse 5?
answers: Sanctify yourselves
Pray all day
Go out to the nearest camp
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says 'Sanctify yourselves' — to prepare or purify for what is coming.

easy.question: Who carried the ark of the covenant in verse 6?
answers: The people
The priests
Moses
easy.explanation: The verse records '...the priests... took up the ark of the covenant and went before the people' — the priests carried it.

easy.question: What did the LORD say he would do among them tomorrow according to verse 5?
answers: Send rain
Break down walls
Do wonders among you
easy.explanation: The verse states 'Tomorrow the LORD will do wonders among you' — miraculous deeds are promised.

medium.question: Why were the priests commanded to 'stand still in Jordan' when they reached the brink?
answers: To stand in the water until everyone had crossed
To make an offering to idols there
To measure the depth of the Jordan
medium.explanation: Verse 8 instructs the priests to stand in the river at the brink while the people pass — to remain until all have crossed.

medium.question: What does the word 'wonders' mean in the phrase 'the LORD will do wonders among you'?
answers: Ordinary, routine things
Great, miraculous deeds
Laws and judgments
medium.explanation: 'Wonders' here describes extraordinary, miraculous acts — supernatural interventions by God.

medium.question: What was the order of actions in verse 6?
answers: The people carried the ark before the priests
The priests carried the ark but went after the people
The priests carried the ark and went before the people
medium.explanation: Verse 6 says the priests took up the ark and went before the people — the priests led the way.

challenge.question: What is the practical effect of the promise 'as I was with Moses, so I will be with thee' on Joshua's status?
answers: God will continue to be present and support Joshua as he did Moses
Joshua will receive Moses' powers in a physical sense
The people will stop remembering Moses and focus only on Joshua
challenge.explanation: The promise stresses continuity of God's presence and support, legitimizing Joshua's leadership as Moses' successor.

challenge.question: Why was carrying the ark before the people important in the ancient religious-cultural context?
answers: A way to hide the ark from enemies
The ark signified the LORD's presence and showed that divine leadership and protection led the people
The ark served as a device for measuring distances
challenge.explanation: In the biblical tradition the ark symbolizes God's presence; carrying it before the people signaled that God led and protected them.

challenge.question: How should the command 'ye shall stand still in Jordan' in verse 8 be understood practically?
answers: To stand on the riverbank without entering the water
To drain Jordan's water to ease crossing
To stand in the water up to the brim until all the people had crossed
challenge.explanation: The instruction is that the priests should stand in the water (at the brink) until everyone had passed — not to perform construction or drainage.

answers: God will continue to be present and support Joshua as he did Moses

The people will stop remembering Moses and focus only on Joshua
questions.explanation: The promise stresses continuity of God's presence and support, legitimizing Joshua's leadership as Moses' successor.

answers: A way to hide the ark from enemies

The ark served as a device for measuring distances
questions.explanation: In the biblical tradition the ark symbolizes God's presence; carrying it before the people signaled that God led and protected them.

questions.question: How should the command 'ye shall stand still in Jordan' in verse 8 be understood practically?
answers: To stand on the riverbank without entering the water
To drain Jordan's water to ease crossing
To stand in the water up to the brim until all the people had crossed
questions.explanation: The instruction is that the priests should stand in the water (at the brink) until everyone had passed — not to perform construction or drainage.

paragraphs.title: The LORD will dispossess the nations

easy.question: Who spoke to the Israelites in verse 9?
answers: Moses
Joshua
Samuel
easy.explanation: The verse opens 'And Joshua said' — Joshua is the speaker.

easy.question: What did Joshua say they would know according to verse 10?
answers: That God lives and will drive out the inhabitants of the land before you
That God will abandon them
That God will destroy the temple
easy.explanation: Verse 10 declares 'the living God is among you, and he will drive out before you...' — God will act to dispossess the nations.

easy.question: What passes before them according to verse 11?
answers: A red heifer
The angel of the LORD alone
The ark of the covenant
easy.explanation: Verse 11 explicitly says 'Behold, the ark of the covenant... passeth over before you into Jordan.'

medium.question: Why does Joshua say 'Come hither, and hear' in verse 9?
answers: So that they may hear the LORD's words and rally around the command
To prepare them for immediate battle
To count the soldiers
medium.explanation: The call invites the people to come and listen to the LORD's words — a summons to attention and unity around the command.

medium.question: What does 'the covenant' refer to in the phrase 'Behold, the ark of the covenant'?
answers: A political treaty between nations
A regular container for tools
The sacred relationship between the LORD and Israel — the ark representing it and containing the tablets
medium.explanation: 'The covenant' here refers to the sacred covenant between God and Israel; the ark is its physical symbol and contains the tablets.

medium.question: What fact does verse 10 state regarding God's involvement in the affairs of the people?
answers: That God lives among them and participates in the conquest of the land
That God will never join them
That God is unrelated to wars
medium.explanation: Verse 10 states 'the living God is among you, and he will drive out...' — God is present and actively involved.

challenge.question: What is the theological significance of the phrase 'the living God is among you' in this context?
answers: That it is a living God, not an idol, who leads and accompanies the people
That the God literally lives inside the people's tents
That God needs food and offerings to remain alive
challenge.explanation: The expression emphasizes that God is living and active, unlike powerless idols; He leads and brings salvation.

challenge.question: According to the verses, who leads the people as they cross the Jordan and enter the land?
answers: The military leaders of the people
The ark of the covenant which passes before them
The elders of the tribes
challenge.explanation: Verse 11 says the ark passes over before them into Jordan — the ark symbolically leads the people.

challenge.question: Which of the following nations is not mentioned in verse 10 as one who will be driven out before them?
answers: The Amorite
The Canaanite
The Moabite
challenge.explanation: Verse 10 lists Canaanites, Hittites, Hivites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Amorites, and Jebusites; the Moabites are not mentioned.

questions.question: What is the theological significance of the phrase 'the living God is among you' in this context?
answers: That it is a living God, not an idol, who leads and accompanies the people
That the God literally lives inside the people's tents
That God needs food and offerings to remain alive
questions.explanation: The expression emphasizes that God is living and active, unlike powerless idols; He leads and brings salvation.

questions.question: According to the verses, who leads the people as they cross the Jordan and enter the land?
answers: The military leaders of the people
The ark of the covenant which passes before them
The elders of the tribes
questions.explanation: Verse 11 says the ark passes over before them into Jordan — the ark symbolically leads the people.

questions.question: Which of the following nations is not mentioned in verse 10 as one who will be driven out before them?
answers: The Amorite
The Canaanite
The Moabite
questions.explanation: Verse 10 lists Canaanites, Hittites, Hivites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Amorites, and Jebusites; the Moabites are not mentioned.

paragraphs.title: Twelve chosen men and the sign of the waters

easy.question: Who was taken according to verse 12?
answers: Twelve men — one from each tribe
Only the priests
All the people of Israel
easy.explanation: Verse 12 says 'Now therefore take you twelve men... one man out of every tribe' — twelve men, one per tribe.

easy.question: From what source were the waters stopped according to the verse?
answers: The great sea
The Jordan
The Nile
easy.explanation: The verse specifies 'the waters of Jordan' — it is the Jordan River.

easy.question: What will happen to the waters when the priests' feet rest?
answers: The waters will soak into the ground
The waters will continue to flow as usual
The waters will be cut off and stand in one heap
easy.explanation: The verse says the waters that come down from above shall be cut off and 'stand upon an heap' — the flow will be halted and piled up.

medium.question: Why were exactly twelve men taken according to the context?
answers: To represent all the tribes of Israel
To establish a temporary camp on the Jordan
To serve as a military force
medium.explanation: The wording 'one man out of every tribe' shows they were chosen as symbolic representatives of each tribe.

medium.question: What does the word 'heap' mean in the phrase 'and they shall stand upon an heap'?
answers: A small boat or ark on the water
A pile/mass of standing water
A waterfall
medium.explanation: 'Heap' here refers to a piling up or mass — the waters accumulating into a mound rather than flowing.

medium.question: Who were the bearers of the ark as said in verse 13?
answers: The elders of the tribes
Heads of families
The priests who bore the ark
medium.explanation: Verse 13 refers to the 'feet of the priests that bare the ark' — the priests are the bearers.

challenge.question: What is the effect of the title 'Lord of all the earth' in the context of the miracle?
answers: It expresses God's sovereignty over the whole earth and power to control nature (for example rivers)
It emphasizes that the Lord is a local king of Canaan only
It refers only to ownership of the ark
challenge.explanation: The title stresses God's rule over all the earth, so stopping the river demonstrates His authority over nature.

challenge.question: Which part of the river is meant by 'the waters which come down from above'?
answers: Underground springs that feed the river
The waters flowing downstream from upstream sources (the normal current)
Standing waters on the banks only
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to the river's normal downstream current — the waters coming from upstream sources.

challenge.question: What does the phrase that the waters 'come down from above' suggest about the season and difficulty of crossing?
answers: That it indicates drought and low water
That it was the calm summer season
That it was the flood season/peak flow, so crossing would be difficult and required a miracle
challenge.explanation: Referring to waters 'coming down from above' implies strong upstream flow (flood/peak), making crossing hazardous and necessitating a miraculous intervention.

questions.question: What is the effect of the title 'Lord of all the earth' in the context of the miracle?
answers: It expresses God's sovereignty over the whole earth and power to control nature (for example rivers)
It emphasizes that the Lord is a local king of Canaan only
It refers only to ownership of the ark
questions.explanation: The title stresses God's rule over all the earth, so stopping the river demonstrates His authority over nature.

questions.question: Which part of the river is meant by 'the waters which come down from above'?
answers: Underground springs that feed the river
The waters flowing downstream from upstream sources (the normal current)
Standing waters on the banks only
questions.explanation: The phrase refers to the river's normal downstream current — the waters coming from upstream sources.

questions.question: What does the phrase that the waters 'come down from above' suggest about the season and difficulty of crossing?
answers: That it indicates drought and low water
That it was the calm summer season
That it was the flood season/peak flow, so crossing would be difficult and required a miracle
questions.explanation: Referring to waters 'coming down from above' implies strong upstream flow (flood/peak), making crossing hazardous and necessitating a miraculous intervention.

paragraphs.title: Departure to the Jordan and the priests' entry

easy.question: Who carried the ark before the people when they went to cross the Jordan?
answers: The priests bearing the ark
Moses and Joshua
The tribes of Israel
easy.explanation: The verse states 'the priests bearing the ark before the people' — the priests led the way.

easy.question: What happened to the priests' feet when they reached the Jordan?
answers: They remained dry
They were dipped in the water
They were injured
easy.explanation: The text notes 'the feet of the priests that bare the ark were dipped in the brim of the water' — their feet were immersed.

easy.question: Where did the people go after they crossed the Jordan according to the verse?
answers: To the Red Sea
To another unspecified place
Right against Jericho
easy.explanation: The verse ends 'and the people passed over right against Jericho' — they crossed opposite Jericho.

medium.question: What does 'an heap' mean in the context 'and they shall stand upon an heap'?
answers: A pile of water in one place
A single person who helped the people
A single wave that flowed swiftly
medium.explanation: In context the waters 'stood' and gathered — 'an heap' refers to the accumulation of water in one place.

medium.question: Why is the Jordan described as 'overflowing all his banks at harvest'?
answers: Because many people were passing there
Because of a sudden rain
Because it was the harvest season and the river was full
medium.explanation: The verse notes 'for Jordan overfloweth all his banks at the time of harvest' — at harvest the river is full, making it high.

medium.question: What happened when the priests stood on the brink of the water holding the ark?
answers: The waters continued to flow as usual
The waters stood still and made a crossing, then the people crossed
The ark sank and the ritual was broken
medium.explanation: When the priests' feet touched the water the current was stopped and a crossing formed; then the people passed.

challenge.question: When the verse calls the 'salt sea' the 'sea of the plain'—what place is meant and why is it important to the crossing?
answers: The blue sea in northern Galilee, unrelated to the crossing
A large lake west of Shechem
The low sea southeast of Jericho (the Dead Sea); mentioning it defines the area where the waters were stopped
challenge.explanation: The 'sea of the plain' refers to the Dead Sea; the reference helps define the geographic extent of the miracle.

challenge.question: What does the phrase 'the waters which came down from above' mean regarding the nature of the stoppage?
answers: From the source/upstream of the flow; this suggests the stoppage began upstream and the waters piled up there
'Upon the rock'; suggests the waters broke against a rock
Outside the channel; suggests the waters vanished into side channels
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates the river's upstream flow was halted — the stoppage began above, causing the waters to accumulate upstream.

challenge.question: What is the symbolic meaning of the priests entering the water while carrying the ark?
answers: To show the priests wanted to avoid responsibility
The priests acted as spiritual leaders — a meeting point between the people and God, and their action produced a miracle that opened the way
It signaled that the ark had lost its holiness
challenge.explanation: The priests, as carriers of the ark, acted as spiritual intermediaries; their standing in the water accompanied the divine act that opened the path.

questions.question: When the verse calls the 'salt sea' the 'sea of the plain'—what place is meant and why is it important to the crossing?
answers: The blue sea in northern Galilee, unrelated to the crossing
A large lake west of Shechem
The low sea southeast of Jericho (the Dead Sea); mentioning it defines the area where the waters were stopped
questions.explanation: The 'sea of the plain' refers to the Dead Sea; the reference helps define the geographic extent of the miracle.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'the waters which came down from above' mean regarding the nature of the stoppage?
answers: From the source/upstream of the flow; this suggests the stoppage began upstream and the waters piled up there
'Upon the rock'; suggests the waters broke against a rock
Outside the channel; suggests the waters vanished into side channels
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates the river's upstream flow was halted — the stoppage began above, causing the waters to accumulate upstream.

questions.question: What is the symbolic meaning of the priests entering the water while carrying the ark?
answers: To show the priests wanted to avoid responsibility
The priests acted as spiritual leaders — a meeting point between the people and God, and their action produced a miracle that opened the way
It signaled that the ark had lost its holiness
questions.explanation: The priests, as carriers of the ark, acted as spiritual intermediaries; their standing in the water accompanied the divine act that opened the path.

paragraphs.title: The waters stood and the people passed

easy.question: Who stood when the ark was in Jordan?
answers: The priests bearing the ark
Joshua and his sons
All the people
easy.explanation: The verse states 'And the priests that bare the ark... stood firm on dry ground' — the priests stood.

easy.question: Where did the priests who bore the ark stand?
answers: On top of the hill near Israel's camp
In the dry ground within the Jordan
In the temple
easy.explanation: The verse says they stood 'on dry ground in the midst of Jordan' — i.e., in the riverbed on dry ground.

easy.question: What did all Israel do while the priests stood in the dry place?
answers: They waited outside the camp
They passed through the dry ground until everyone had crossed the Jordan
They offered sacrifices there
easy.explanation: The verse reports 'and all the Israelites passed over on dry ground, until all the people were passed clean over Jordan' — they crossed while the priests stood.

medium.question: What does the word 'dry ground' mean in the context 'on dry ground in the midst of Jordan'?
answers: A dry place inside the riverbed where the waters were held back
A storm of thunder and wind within the river
A small village on the riverbank
medium.explanation: The context indicates there was exposed dry ground within the riverbed where the waters had been held back, allowing passage.

medium.question: Who passed through the dry ground according to the verse?
answers: Only the priests carrying the ark
All Israel
Only the tribe of Judah
medium.explanation: The verse clearly states 'all Israel' passed over on dry ground.

medium.question: What does the phrase 'until all the people were passed clean over Jordan' mean?
answers: The priests left before most people crossed
They stood there until the entire nation finished crossing the river
The people turned back and then crossed again
medium.explanation: The phrase indicates the priests remained until every person had completed the crossing.

challenge.question: What follows from the writers' phrase about the dry ground within the Jordan—what happened to the river's waters during the crossing?
answers: The Jordan's waters were held back allowing dry ground for crossing
The Jordan became a deeper lake
The people dug a large channel to cross
challenge.explanation: Describing a 'dry ground in the midst of Jordan' implies the river's flow was arrested so the bed was exposed for crossing — a miraculous stoppage.

challenge.question: In the traditional context of the book of Joshua, near which city did the Jordan crossing described in this chapter take place?
answers: Near Jericho
At Sinai
At Shiloh
challenge.explanation: The crossing is described as taking place opposite Jericho — the narrative places the event near Jericho.

challenge.question: Why did the priests bearing the ark stand on the dry ground instead of moving forward immediately?
answers: So as not to frighten the people with the ark
So that the ark would be an active sign of God's presence and protect the people during the crossing
To build a wall around the camp
challenge.explanation: Their standing with the ark indicated the ark's role as the visible sign of God's presence and safeguarding during the crossing.

questions.question: What follows from the writers' phrase about the dry ground within the Jordan—what happened to the river's waters during the crossing?
answers: The Jordan's waters were held back allowing dry ground for crossing
The Jordan became a deeper lake
The people dug a large channel to cross
questions.explanation: Describing a 'dry ground in the midst of Jordan' implies the river's flow was arrested so the bed was exposed for crossing — a miraculous stoppage.

answers: Near Jericho
At Sinai
At Shiloh
questions.explanation: The crossing is described as taking place opposite Jericho — the narrative places the event near Jericho.

answers: So as not to frighten the people with the ark
So that the ark would be an active sign of God's presence and protect the people during the crossing
To build a wall around the camp
questions.explanation: Their standing with the ark indicated the ark's role as the visible sign of God's presence and safeguarding during the crossing.

verses_kjv: And Joshua rose early in the morning; and they removed from Shittim, and came to Jordan, he and all the children of Israel, and lodged there before they passed over.
And it came to pass after three days, that the officers went through the host;
And they commanded the people, saying, When ye see the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God, and the priests the Levites bearing it, then ye shall remove from your place, and go after it.
Yet there shall be a space between you and it, about two thousand cubits by measure: come not near unto it, that ye may know the way by which ye must go: for ye have not passed this way heretofore.
And Joshua said unto the people, Sanctify yourselves: for to morrow the Lord will do wonders among you.
And Joshua spake unto the priests, saying, Take up the ark of the covenant, and pass over before the people. And they took up the ark of the covenant, and went before the people.
And the Lord said unto Joshua, This day will I begin to magnify thee in the sight of all Israel, that they may know that, as I was with Moses, so I will be with thee.
And thou shalt command the priests that bear the ark of the covenant, saying, When ye are come to the brink of the water of Jordan, ye shall stand still in Jordan.
And Joshua said unto the children of Israel, Come hither, and hear the words of the Lord your God.

And Joshua said, Hereby ye shall know that the living God is among you, and that he will without fail drive out from before you the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Hivites, and the Perizzites, and the Girgashites, and the Amorites, and the Jebusites.
Behold, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth passeth over before you into Jordan.
Now therefore take you twelve men out of the tribes of Israel, out of every tribe a man.

And it shall come to pass, as soon as the soles of the feet of the priests that bear the ark of the Lord, the Lord of all the earth, shall rest in the waters of Jordan, that the waters of Jordan shall be cut off from the waters that come down from above; and they shall stand upon an heap.
And it came to pass, when the people removed from their tents, to pass over Jordan, and the priests bearing the ark of the covenant before the people;

And as they that bare the ark were come unto Jordan, and the feet of the priests that bare the ark were dipped in the brim of the water, (for Jordan overfloweth all his banks all the time of harvest,)

That the waters which came down from above stood and rose up upon an heap very far from the city Adam, that is beside Zaretan: and those that came down toward the sea of the plain, even the salt sea, failed, and were cut off: and the people passed over right against Jericho.

And the priests that bare the ark of the covenant of the Lord stood firm on dry ground in the midst of Jordan, and all the Israelites passed over on dry ground, until all the people were passed clean over Jordan.
